We have two little ones, both in diapers still at 6 and 25 months old, so I'm not there yet but the training days are approaching. What I can say is that these little people work through these stages how and when they want and there's a limit on how much direction they will take.

Be consistent in praising each of the 700x the #1 is flushed and also in suggesting the potty as a pull-up alternative then they'll catch on and/or acquiesce eventually.

When we first started potty training I would give my son 1 chocolate chip for going pee pee in the potty and two for pooping. Later, when pooping became more of an issue I started giving him a jumbo marshmallow as a reward. Also, when he has "lapses?" and is fighting me on pooping in the potty I will take away his privilege to pick the movie or kid's show we watch that day. I hope this can help you somewhat! :)

Sooo call me crazy. Rewards/Treats. My niece is being potty trained and she has he own candy jar and every time she goes potty she get 1 treat from the jar of her choosing. Its been working great so far, almost too great where she wants to go to the potty now.

Ok now I am getting crazy. Have they seen you do the poo?

I'm an old guy with five grown children. When we were going through this challenge, the solution we hit upon was to put them in regular underwear and let them do whatever they did. Thing is, they only got one pair per day and if they went in them, they got to sit in them until whatever substance was expelled from whichever orifice became cold. Probably considered child abuse now, though.

Have you asked your pediatrician for approved tactics?
We did pants-free for two days. No floor messes, and it totally ended the game of "hold it until there's a diaper on." You've just got to go for it!
If they poo where they aren't supposed to, rub their nose in it.

You have to figure out what the one thing is that will tip the scales. Purchase that one thing. Put it in top of the refrigerator and tell them it's their potty reward. Once they've gone in the potty for a week they can have it.

Start a sticker chart. Stick to your guns. If they miss a day then back to square one. Don't make a big deal, just say oops we have to start over!

One of my twins took a bit longer, but as soon as we figured out what would do it then it was cake.
